identification.summary: TA530 is Proofpoint's designator for a financially motivated actor that, since January 2016, targeted executives and other senior employees with personalized phishing email, often in campaigns limited to a single industry vertical [S1][S2].
identification.notes: TA530 is a Proofpoint tracking designation. No Microsoft name or MITRE group was found in the sources gathered. The imported record lists country CN, but no gathered source supports a country of origin; treat that field as unverified.

attribution.confidence: Proofpoint described TA530 as financially motivated; no state sponsor or named individuals appear in the sources gathered [S1][S2].
attribution.basis: Proofpoint campaign observation of personalized email, tailored payloads and recipient targeting [S1][S2].

objectives: Financial gain: the actor sought to infect executives' machines with banking Trojans and ransomware [S1][S2][S3].

sectors: Executives and senior staff across multiple verticals (campaigns often single-vertical) [S1][S2]
Banking customers in Australia (Ursnif ISFB configuration) [S2]
targeting.notes: Proofpoint counted roughly 300,000 personalized messages to organizations in the US, UK and Australia [S1][S2]. Targets typically held titles such as CFO, Head of Finance, Senior Vice President or Director [S1][S2].

capabilities.summary: Large-scale personalized phishing: each message carried the recipient's name, job title, phone number and company name, in some cases verified as accurate by Proofpoint and likely drawn from public sources such as LinkedIn or company sites [S1][S2]. Payloads were tailored by region and industry and reported to include the Ursnif ISFB banking Trojan configured for Australian banks, a fileless Ursnif/RecoLoad point-of-sale reconnaissance Trojan, and CryptoWall ransomware [S1][S2][S3]. Volume was well below Dridex or Locky botnet blasts but large for spear phishing [S2].

campaigns.name: Personalized executive phishing
campaigns.summary: Proofpoint reports TA530 began targeting executives and senior employees with personalized email, roughly 300,000 messages to US, UK and Australian organizations, delivering varied malware [S1][S2].

campaigns.name: Public disclosure of TA530 activity
campaigns.summary: Proofpoint published its analysis and trade press (KnowBe4 dated 2016-04-09) reported TA530 as spear phishing combined with ransomware [S1][S3].

diamond.adversary: Financially motivated actor tracked by Proofpoint as TA530; no identity or sponsor established in gathered sources [S1][S2].
diamond.capability: Personalized phishing using scraped public data; Ursnif ISFB, fileless Ursnif/RecoLoad and CryptoWall payloads [S1][S2][S3].
diamond.victim: Executives and senior finance-titled staff in US, UK and Australian organizations, plus retail and hospitality for POS reconnaissance [S1][S2].
diamond.socioPolitical: Cybercrime profit motive; Proofpoint expected personalization to spread to other actors [S2].
diamond.technology: Email gateways and endpoints of executives; public professional-profile data used for lure personalization [S1][S2].

gaps: Proofpoint primary posts could not be opened (fetch failed); details rely on search-result excerpts and secondary coverage [S1][S2].
The imported reference 'August in December: New Information Stealer Hits the Scene' was not verified to concern TA530 and is not cited.
Country of origin (imported as CN) unsupported; no sponsor, infrastructure, aliases or MITRE mapping found.
Activity after 2016 not found; the actor may have been retired or renamed by Proofpoint.
Exact Proofpoint publication date of the 'Phish Scales' post not confirmed; 2016-04 is inferred from secondary coverage.
